settings.out_of_scope_reason: Offline mechanism-design / one-sided matching problem: planner sees only ordinal preferences, performance measured by distortion and incentive ratio; no learning.
unmapped: n strategic agents matched to s services over T rounds
planner observes only ordinal reports (once, before matching)
matched services are blocked for D_{i,j}-1 rounds (known delays)
reward profiles in the probability simplex (unit-sum)
performance measured by distortion (worst-case ratio vs optimal feasible matching sequence) and incentive ratio
settings.definition_quote: In this setting, the planner must produce a feasible matching sequence of length $T$. Prior to the selection of a matching sequence, each agent submits a linear preference ordering to the planner.

settings.name_in_paper: Online SBM setting with bandit feedback
unmapped: n strategic agents matched to s services each round (one-sided matching)
planner sees only agents' ordinal reports, not rewards
matched services blocked for known agent-service-dependent delays D_{i,j}, max delay D_tilde
agents are mean-based (preference ordering by empirical means)
regret measured against alpha times the optimal offline feasible matching sequence (dynamic alpha-regret)
settings.definition_quote: At the end of each time step, agent $i$ receives a reward, $r_{i,t} \in [0, 1]$, sampled from a distribution with mean $\mu_{i,j}$, where $j$ is the service agent $i$ was assigned in the matching returned by the planner.

source.label: thm: distortion of deterministic policies
source.quote: The distortion of any deterministic policy is $\Omega(s)$.

results.notes: Bound on distortion (multiplicative ratio), not regret.

source.label: thm:sqrt distortion
source.quote: The distortion of the best randomised policy is $\Omega(\sqrt{s})$.

source.label: thm:distortion of RRSD
source.quote: The distortion of \texttt{RRSD} is at most $O(\sqrt{s})$.

results.notes: Distortion upper bound under truthful reporting.

tuning: set of 4n^2 log(n) permutations from Lemma 1

source.label: thm:det-upper
source.quote: There is an admissible deterministic policy with distortion at most $O(s)$ for any $T \geq O(n^{2}\log(n))$

results.notes: Proof gives distortion at most 4n = O(s). Deterministic, achieved by DRRSD.

source.label: thm: incentive ratio of RRSD
source.quote: The incentive ratio of \texttt{RRSD} is asymptotically bounded below by $1 - 1/e$.

results.notes: Incentive ratio guarantee (bounded BELOW by 1-1/e, i.e., a guarantee on truthfulness); recorded as a guarantee with side 'upper' as it is an algorithm guarantee; not regret.

symbols.Delta_min_sbm: min over agents i and service pairs a != b of |mu_{i,a} - mu_{i,b}|

tuning: exploration: each agent-service pair assigned ceil(2 log(2Tsn)/Delta_min^2) times

source.label: thm:bandit
source.quote: Under the assumption that agents are mean-based, the following is true for all $\mu$ and $D$: (i) The dynamic $(1/\sqrt{s})$-regret of \texttt{BRRSD} is $O\left(\tilde{D}\sqrt{s}\log\left(Tsn\right)/\Delta^{2}_{\text{min}}\right)$.

results.notes: Dynamic alpha-regret with alpha = 1/sqrt(s), against the optimal feasible matching sequence. Delta_min differs from canonical (gap between any two services of the same agent).

symbols.Delta_min_sbm: min over agents i and service pairs a != b of |mu_{i,a} - mu_{i,b}|

tuning: exploration: each agent-service pair assigned ceil(2 log(2Tsn)/Delta_min^2) times

source.label: thm:bandit
source.quote: (ii) The $(1-1/e)$-IC regret for all agents under \texttt{BRRSD} is $O\left(\tilde{D}s\log\left(Tsn\right)/\Delta^{2}_{\text{min}}\right)$.

results.notes: (1-1/e)-incentive-compatible regret of each agent (gain from misreporting), not standard regret.
